description: "What was that moving light?" Given where and when a light was seen, lists the satellites that were sunlit, above the horizon and within `tolerance` degrees of that spot, best match first, from every satellite in the catalog (active satellites plus CelesTrak's visual group). Needs the Sun at least about 3 degrees below the horizon. A match must lie within tolerance of the reported spot (azimuth or direction, plus elevation); travel never adds a match, it only re-ranks them by how well each one's direction of travel agrees. Sightings by eye are often 10 to 20 degrees off, so widen tolerance before concluding nothing matched. Each candidate has its azimuth, elevation, angular error, direction of travel, magnitude (estimated where none is measured, see magnitudeEstimated), name and a url to its page. Satellites whose orbital elements are more than 14 days from the sighting time are left out and counted (skippedStaleElements). If the sky was too bright then, a note says so instead of a list; with no match, a note suggests checking the time and direction or widening tolerance. For satellites up at this moment use find_satellites_up_now; for upcoming passes use find_passes or find_best_pass.

azimuth.description: where it was, in degrees from north (90 = east), 0 to 360. Give this or direction.

direction.description: where it was, as a compass word: N, NNE, NE, ... or "north-east".

elevation.description: how high it was, in degrees above the horizon (0 to 90, 90 = straight up). Required.

lat.description: observer latitude in decimal degrees, north positive (-90 to 90). Give it with lon, or give location instead.

limit.description: how many candidates to return, 1 to 10. Default 5.

location.description: where the observer is, when lat and lon are not given (they win when both are): a Maidenhead grid square (EN52, EN52ve, EN52ve12), coordinates in any common form ("41.88, -87.63", "41.88N 87.63W", "41°52'48"N 87°37'48"W", a Google Maps link or geo: URI), all read locally, or a place name (city, address, landmark) looked up with OpenStreetMap. Prefer lat and lon, or a grid square, when you have them: a place name is a network lookup.

lon.description: observer longitude in decimal degrees, east positive and west negative (-180 to 180).

passTime.description: old name for time; still accepted.

time.description: time of the sighting. Default: now. ISO 8601 with Z or an offset, e.g. "2026-11-14T21:00:00-06:00"; a time with no offset, e.g. "2026-11-14T21:00", is read in the observer's time zone, and the result echoes how it was read (interpretedAs). A local time the clocks skip at a daylight-saving change is moved forward, with a note.

tolerance.description: how far off the reported spot a match may be, in degrees, 1 to 45. Default 10.

travel.description: the compass direction it was moving towards, e.g. "NE". Optional, but it sharpens the match.

name: identify_satellite
title: Identify a satellite
